(p. 86) Surat al-Qamar (The Moon)

Its central theme is the explanation of the end of the sequence (al-Najm) concerning the Hour: its certainty, how near it is, and the classification of its people. This is in light of what was mentioned there about the wonder of the Qur'an, laughter and weeping, and action. It is addressed to the seeker of knowledge who is guided by it, and to the one who follows his own desires and appetites and is lost through neglect, so he is a failure. This is because Allah, glory be to Him, promised this through the information given by His Prophet (ﷺ), and its truth was confirmed by the signs He strengthened him with, by which His power to create and to annihilate what He wills was established. Thus His sole sovereignty was proven. He also confirmed the nearness of the Hour through the effect upon the sign of the night, which indicates the power to undo the heavens, which entails destruction... For that [is so]... because only the effect of the sign of the day remains, and when it is folded up, and there is general ruin, which announces the gathering before the One, the Subduer. The most indicative of this entire purpose is its first verse. Therefore it was named after what it contains of nearness (al-iqtirab), the Hour, and the moon. Its naming after the moon was more famous, because the moon by its swift course and its frequent changing indicates the nearness that the star (al-najm) was used to indicate, by allusion and not by explicit statement. It was not named "The Splitting" because when that is mentioned alone it refers to the name [of the moon], whereas the sky has a better claim to it.

(In the name of Allah), whose knowledge encompasses all things, so His power is complete; (the Most Merciful), whose mercy embraces everything, so it covers both the wretched and the blessed; (the Most Compassionate), who specially granted the completion of blessing to whom He chose, so His mercy made them happy.

* *

When the sequence was concluded with a warning of the approach of the Resurrection, which they deny, after it had opened with the oaths in the sequence, which is more general than the moon and others by its movement in rising, setting, ascending and descending, this surah opened with that, together with the indication of it by reason and by revelation regarding its effect on the greatest of Allah's signs and other things, so that He might cut His servants off from corruption and they might prepare for it before its coming in the best preparation. He said, indicating His great power over it by feminizing its verb: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾. (Al-Sa'ah, the Hour): the instant after which there is, in reality, no other hour, in which the Resurrection will take place. This is because little remains between us and it, compared with the time that passed from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until the sending of the Seal of the Prophets, after whose community no community remains to be awaited. Thus there is in time a respite for that.

Since the announcement of its nearness needs, for the stubborn opponent, a sign indicating it, and since heavenly signs are greater, and the effect upon them is more indicative of complete power, and since the moon is more indicative of the seasons by which people's livelihoods are provided, and the Arabs were the most knowledgeable of people about them, He showed them the effect upon it, [indicating] the nearness of [the Hour] together with a warning of the severe punishment, by the destruction of the causes. So He said: ﴿And the moon has split﴾, with the utmost speed and ease, ﴿as a sign for the Messenger who warns you﴾ by it. Its splitting, together with the indication of that through the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and other things, was also an indication of its occurrence and its nearness, by a great effect that breaks the custom of what came before it, an effect upon one of the two luminaries which are the greatest causes established for livelihoods. This indicates the power to affect [them] in the Hereafter, and that in turn indicates the power over complete disposal of both, by gathering them, eclipsing them, and setting them ablaze, and over their cause, which is among the causes of the ruin of the earth. Man will say at that time: "Where is the refuge?" (Qiyamah) announces the folding up of the world, and informs that it has a Lord who acts by choice and governs by wisdom,

(p. 88) and indicates the resurrection of His servants so that He may judge between them concerning what they used to differ about, rewarding whoever followed His messengers and punishing whoever opposed them. The splitting of the moon in its literal sense in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) is a very famous matter, and the consensus (ijma') of the people of tafsir (exegesis) upon it is as stated by al-Qushayri, who said: "It was narrated by Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and there is no dissenter regarding it." End of quotation. The reason is that "Quraysh asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the splitting of the moon in such a way that one part rose on the right side of Hira' and another on its left." This was narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Ibn Mas'ud and Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both. It is known that the Ummah received their two books with acceptance, so it nearly reaches the level of mutawatir (widely transmitted), and the Qur'an has confirmed it, so no doubt remains concerning it. Al-Qushayri said: Ibn 'Umar, Hudhayfah, Ibn 'Abbas and Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with them, also narrated it. Abu Hayyan said: The occasion of its revelation was that the polytheist Arabs from Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you are truthful, then split the moon for us into two halves," and they promised him that they would believe if he did that. It was the night of the full moon, so he asked his Lord and it split. End of quotation. As for the one who says that what is meant is "it will split," he needs a barrier to turn the past tense away from its literal meaning toward the future, and how could he have that, especially since the literal meaning has been strengthened by the sound and well-known transmission?

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When Allah, glory be to Him, informed them that the final end is to Him, and that upon Him is the other creation, and then the recompense of every soul for what it has sent forward will occur, He informed them, glory be to Him, of the nearness of that and its reckoning, so that whoever He granted success might be restrained. So He, Exalted, said: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Then Surat Sad contained, concerning the obstinacy of the polytheists and the evil of their condition, and their rebuke for worshipping what neither harms nor benefits, what is hardly found in any other [surah] preceding it. After the admonition in the surah before it, and the stirring by signs from which none turns away except one whom Allah has misguided and forsaken, and after that this surah established, upon a foundation, what Surat Sad contained. It left no surah among them free of their rebuke and reproach, as in His saying in al-Zumar: ﴿And those who take protectors other than Him [say]: "We only worship them that they may bring us near to Allah in position"﴾ [al-Zumar 39:3], and His saying: ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills﴾ [al-Zumar 39:4], and His saying: ﴿Say: "It is Allah I worship, sincerely devoted to Him in my religion"﴾ [al-Zumar 39:14], ﴿So worship what you wish other than Him﴾ [al-Zumar 39:15], and His saying, as an example of their condition: ﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another﴾ [al-Zumar 39:29], and so on to what follows of rebuke and reproach. And His saying in Surat Ghafir: ﴿None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ [Ghafir 40:4], and His saying: ﴿That is because, when Allah alone is invoked, you disbelieve; but when partners are associated with Him, you believe. So judgment belongs to Allah﴾ [Ghafir 40:12], and His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth?﴾ [Ghafir 40:82] and so on, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute the signs of Allah without authority that has come to them, there is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir 40:56], and His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir 40:69], ﴿Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers, they are going to know﴾ [Ghafir 40:70], to His saying: ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir 40:77], and His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth?﴾ [Ghafir 40:21], and what lies between these verses. And His saying in al-Sajdah: ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾ [Fussilat 41:4], ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are in coverings"﴾ [Fussilat 41:5], ﴿And those who disbelieve said: "Do not listen to this Qur'an and talk over it [with noise]"﴾ [Fussilat 41:26], ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs are not hidden from Us﴾ [Fussilat 41:40], to His saying: ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾ [Fussilat 41:44], and His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [Fussilat 41:53], to the end of the surah. And His saying in al-Shura: ﴿And those who take protectors other than Him, Allah is Guardian over them, and you are not over them a manager﴾ [al-Shura 42:6], ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them﴾ [al-Shura 42:13], ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is void with their Lord﴾ [al-Shura 42:16], and the verse: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them of the religion that which Allah has not permitted?﴾ [al-Shura 42:21], and the verse: ﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them; your duty is only to convey﴾ [al-Shura 42:48], and His saying in al-Zukhruf: ﴿Shall We turn away from you the reminder, disregarding you [because] you are a transgressing people?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:5], and so on.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 1 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And they have ascribed to Him a portion from among His servants﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 15], up to what recurs in this surah of rebukes with which they were reproached most severely. It is repeated in many verses, so reflect upon them, such as His saying in ad-Dukhan, ﴿Nay, they are in doubt, playing﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 9], up to His saying, ﴿On the day We seize with the greatest seizing, indeed We will take retribution﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 16]. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for them all﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 40], up to His saying, ﴿This is what you used to doubt﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 50]. And His saying in al-Jathiyah, "Then in what statement after this will they believe?" up to His saying, ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord, for them is a painful punishment of wretchedness﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 11]. And His saying, ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his deity his own desire?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23], to the end of the surah. And His saying in al-Ahqaf, ﴿And those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3]. Most of this verse [i.e., the verse in question] does not depart from this theme up to its conclusion. The same is true of surah Muhammad, which contains nothing but the command to kill them, take them captive and hasten war against them: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [strike] the necks﴾ [Muhammad: 4]. As for surah al-Fath, what it contains of glad tidings and conquest is more grievous to the disbelievers than everything with which they were reproached, and it does not depart from the aforementioned aim. Likewise surah al-Hujurat, because it contains commands regarding the honouring and reverence of the Prophet (ﷺ), which gladden the eye of the believer and kill the hostile envier, and also what it contains of the dissolution of the affairs of the disbelievers, the unification of the believers' word and their brotherhood. The effect of this is not hidden from anyone. As for surah adh-Dhariyat, at-Tur and an-Najm, what they contain of what we mentioned earlier is most clear, and every surah among them opens with this. So reflect upon their openings, for in that is sufficiency regarding the aim.

And Allah the Exalted is most knowing of what is correct. When what He intended of reproaching the deniers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached its utmost limit, and the verses in this surah reached the extreme of that, their falsehood became pure and their root was cut off. They could not answer what He, glory be to Him, presented to them in surah al-Qamar regarding the circumstances of the nations with their prophets. The intent of that, and Allah knows best, was merely to make known that they were admonished, so they denied, and so they were seized, in order that it would be clear to these people that there is no difference between them and others, and that the great forbearance of Him, glory be to Him, toward them should not deceive them. So this surah is a final warning (i'dhar) after their rebuke and the severing of their argument by what preceded, and after the matter of their admonition and alerting, with every verse, reached a limit that humans cannot match. For this reason, He, glory be to Him, opened this surah with His saying, ﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news that which contains a deterrent﴾ [al-Qamar: 4], ﴿perfect wisdom, but warnings do not avail﴾ [al-Qamar: 5]. And He concluded it with His saying, ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those? Or is there for you an exemption in the scriptures?﴾ [al-Qamar: 43]. This shows what we have put forward.

It had been said to them, "What difference is there between you and those who came before, that you should commit what they committed and suppose you will succeed with your great reward?" So He, glory be to Him, mentioned to them the story of every nation and its destruction when it denied, with the utmost brevity, the most abundant presentation, the most majestic expression and the most subtle allusion. He began with the story of the people of Nuh, with His saying, ﴿The people of Nuh denied﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 105], up to His saying, ﴿And We have left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 15], ﴿So how was My punishment and warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16]. Then He continued in mentioning the nations [p. 92] with their prophets, as they are mentioned in the surah whose reports of them are narrated, a nation after a nation. However, what occurs here of their stories is more effective in deterring, more eloquent in admonition, and more explicit in disclosing the evil of their outcome and the consequence of their denial. Then every story was concluded with His saying, ﴿So how was My punishment and warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16]. And between these stories He interposed His saying, ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 17]. This is an indication of the removal of the excuse of one who clings to the difficulty of matters against His reminders, admonitions and exhortations, and who claims, after that, that it is obscure. So it is said to him that it is made easy and its aim is near. This applies to what is attained upon alertness and reminder, given what is in him, with acceptance occurring by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Beyond that lies what is intricate and ambiguous, which what He mentioned does not depend upon, and for the general body of believers it is sufficient to have faith in all of it and to act upon its clear (muhkam) rulings. Then Allah the Exalted opens the understanding of that to whom He honours with it and raises in rank, so it becomes clear according to what Allah the Exalted expands his breast for. ﴿Allah will raise those who believe among you and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11].

Among the facilitation of the aforementioned purpose is the repetition of the stories of the prophets with their nations in several surahs, so that whoever memorises any of them comes to know what suffices for taking heed from them. Then, when some of it is combined with some other, there gathers from it what would not have been attained from some one surah alone. Glory be to Him who made it a dazzling proof and an evidence of the truthfulness of the one who brought it, Muhammad (ﷺ), and a straight path and a clear light.

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the consequences of the nations in their denial, He said to the polytheists of the Arabs, ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾ [al-Qamar: 43]. Of this pattern is the saying of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition cause you to sin, lest there befall you like what befell the people of Nuh, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih. And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud: 89]. [p. 93] Then Allah the Exalted said, ﴿Or do they say, "We are a united victorious group"?﴾ [al-Qamar: 44], ﴿The group will be defeated and they will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]. That is, you have clung to your unity and your community, so I will break that by your defeat on the day of Badr through the killing of your chieftains. Then what is your argument after this? The course of the stories in this surah, and the reliance upon making known the condition of those mentioned, is that they denied and opposed, so their denial was followed by their seizure and destruction. Then all of this was followed by turning the speech toward the polytheists of the Arabs, in His saying, ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾ [al-Qamar: 43]. None of the surahs in which stories are mentioned is as thorough in this manner as al-A'raf and Hud. Apparently, in neither of them, nor in anything of that sort, is there a follow-up mentioning the polytheists of the Arabs in the manner stated here. This indicates the completeness of the intended aim of admonition and stirring by mentioning them, and the conclusion of this purpose.

That is because they were first reminded by presenting the conditions of the nations and making known what their affair came to. This was in the form of presenting one who wishes to discipline a group whose attention he holds before any rebellion or obstinacy appears from them. He addresses them gently and does not speak to them as one who is angry with them, but conveys compassion, kindness and the desire for good for them. Then he reminds them of that and repeats it to them time after time, even if between that there occurs what makes clear the gravity of the threat and the severity of the warning. So it is not accompanied by specifying the addressee and turning the speech entirely toward him. Rather, it is by way of allusion and reproach. Then, if he does not show contempt for what preceded and what follows of gentleness, until the admonition is repeated and is not accepted, here is the place of anger and severe warning. Upon this pattern came the surahs in which the conditions of the nations are mentioned, such as surah al-A'raf, Hud, al-Mu'minun, ash-Shu'ara' and as-Saffat. There is no surah among them except that [p. 94] the one after it is more severe in making known and more hopeful in deterrence after making known.

Consider the follow-up to the stories in surah al-A'raf with His saying, ﴿Thus We detail the signs, so that they may return﴾ [al-A'raf: 174], and His saying after a profound admonition, mentioning the one whom He deprived after he was on the verge of success, the one who inclined to the earth and followed his desire. Then He said after that, ﴿So relate the stories, that they may reflect﴾ [al-A'raf: 176]. And His reminding him of the affliction of heedlessness, up to what the surah concludes with. This is clearly of gentleness in admonition. And He said after the stories of surah Hud, ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord﴾ [Hud: 102], the verse. And He said, ﴿So do not be in doubt concerning what these worship﴾ [Hud: 109], up to His saying, ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion without reduction﴾ [Hud: 109]. The repetition of the verse up to the end of the surah corresponds to what was mentioned, and these verses of al-A'raf did not leave any of the gentleness of invitation. And He said in the stories at the end of surah al-Mu'minun, ﴿So leave them in their confusion for a time﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 54], up to His saying, ﴿they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 56]. Then He said, ﴿And they have other deeds besides that, which they are doing﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 63], ﴿until when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, they will immediately cry out﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 64]. The verses continued upon severity of warning, one following another, up to His saying, ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], and His saying after that, ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 117]. He did not explain these verses, but He explained the event after the stories of surah Hud. He said at the end of the stories of ash-Shu'ara', ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 192], up to His saying, as the conclusion of the surah, ﴿And those who wronged will know what return they will be returned to﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 227]. Thus He rebuked them, censured them, and cleared His Prophet (ﷺ) of their supposition, their great falsehood and their fabrication. All of this is censure, even though nothing like it had preceded in the aforementioned surah. Then it is explicit regarding the polytheists of the Arabs, specifying them without [p. 95] allusion or indirection. Then, after each story in this surah, He said, ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 67], which contains threat and warning. And He said at the end of as-Saffat, ﴿So ask them: Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?﴾ [as-Saffat: 149], ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ [as-Saffat: 150], ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their falsehood that they say﴾ [as-Saffat: 151], ﴿"Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars﴾ [as-Saffat: 152]. This is the greatest rebuke and the most severe reproach. Then He, glory be to Him, cleared His Prophet of the slander of their speech, the evil of their conduct and the ugliness of their deeds, with His saying, ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of honour, above what they describe﴾ [as-Saffat: 180].

When they were seized in every manner, and that did not avail them, Allah the Exalted said in surah al-Qamar, ﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news that which contains a deterrent﴾ [al-Qamar: 4], ﴿perfect wisdom, but warnings do not avail﴾ [al-Qamar: 5]. Then He said to His Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿So turn away from them﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]. His command (ﷺ) to abandon them, turn away from them and withdraw from them did not occur except after the stories in the aforementioned surah had been completed and they had been seized in every way. The first command to him (ﷺ) in this regard was in surah as-Sajdah, ﴿So turn away from them and wait, indeed they are waiting﴾ [as-Sajdah: 30]. Then in surah adh-Dhariyat, ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 54], with the most severe warning and the greatest threat, following every story with His saying, ﴿And We have certainly left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 15], and His saying, ﴿So how was My punishment and warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16]. Then He turned toward them, with what preceded, His saying, ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those, or is there for you an exemption in the scriptures?﴾ [al-Qamar: 43]. So this reached the greatest extent in clarity and in giving excuse. Then Allah the Exalted said, ﴿And everything they did is in the scriptures﴾ [al-Qamar: 52]. So He, glory be to Him, distinguished them by His preceding wisdom concerning them, ﴿Indeed, all things We created with predestination﴾ [al-Qamar: 49]. The mention of the stories ended, and He did not return to them in full in this manner afterward until the end of the Book.

So glory be to Him who showed mercy to His righteous servants through it, made it a dazzling sign, and what a dazzling sign until the Day of Judgement, and cut off the stubbornness of the deniers and the malice of the transgressors, and made it a sufficient explanation, a guiding light, and a healing admonisher. May Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, make us among those who are guided by it and hold fast to its cause. Indeed He is the One worthy of response, pardon and forgiveness. The end.

When the sense was: the disbelievers turned away from the sign of his splitting [the moon] and said, "It is magic," even though they knew that it clearly indicated the truth of the one whose splitting was a confirmation of him, he followed it with an announcement of their state in the future. This was to wean away anyone among the believers who sought to grant one of their proposals in hope of their faith. So he said: ﴿And if they see﴾, i.e., in what is to come, ﴿a sign﴾, whatever sign it might be, ﴿they turn away﴾, i.e., from benefiting from it, just as they turned away from this one when they saw it. Some of them said, "It is magic," and some of them said, "Wait until the travellers (al-Suffar) arrive. If they say that they saw it as you saw it, then it is not magic, for Muhammad cannot bewitch all the people of the earth." So the travellers came and testified that they had seen it split, yet despite that they did not believe. ﴿And they say﴾, i.e., in a manner of renewal and continuity on their part, "This is ﴿magic﴾", i.e., this which this man brings us is from the valley of imagination that has no reality. And it is ﴿continuous (mustamirr)﴾, i.e., because it differs from magic in that it is not revealed at once; rather it is firm, lasting and enduring, by its comprehensiveness and its encompassing of all kinds. For this reason, there results from it the utmost of extraordinary events, which are diverse in kind and numerous.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 3:

When He had weaned them from eagerly anticipating their answer to their demands, according to what I have determined, He consequently mentioned, concerning them regarding the splitting of the moon, His words: ﴿And they denied﴾, meaning: [they denied] that the splitting was a sign indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ), and they resolutely insisted on denial out of obstinacy (ʿinād) or wickedness (khubth) on their part. Since denial in itself may sometimes be correct, He said, clarifying that it is false, and then described their state with His words: ﴿And they followed﴾, meaning: by treating their original upright natural disposition (fiṭar) so that it was turned away from its call to affirmation, ﴿their desires﴾, meaning: until their intellects rejected what the original disposition had guided them to after the natural disposition. Al-Qushayrī said: When the following of desire occurs, from its ill effect denial follows, because Allah, glorified and exalted, confounds the heart of its possessor so that he does not perceive right guidance. And following what is pleasing is accompanied by affirmation, because by the blessings of following the truth, Allah, exalted is He, opens the eye of insight, and so one arrives at affirmation, and Allah is the Guide.

When that was dreadful to the hearts of those who seek the truth, He consoled them by reaching a station where realities become manifest and vain disputations vanish, so He said, connecting it to what is implied by the context: Thus the matter of each of the truthful and the falsifier will be settled in its place, and its minute details and secrets will be disclosed: ﴿And every matter﴾ among your affairs and others ﴿is settled﴾, meaning: established and existing, its end reaching a goal in which its reality becomes manifest without any stratagem accompanying it to reverse that settlement, and it is not hidden from anyone. So the truth will necessarily reach its conclusion in everything, including the appointed terms, guidances, misguidances, felicities, miseries and other things, so that it becomes firmly established with a permanence that has no cessation; and falsehood will reach the end to which the creatures' desires have driven it, so that it vanishes with a vanishing that has no permanence in any respect. When matters are settled, what they have is manifest, and they know the loser from the winner. In a similar context, Ibn ʿAmr al-Taymī, brother of al-Qaʿqāʿ, said regarding the battle of al-Sī in the lands of Iraq:

"Death is our horse when we meet with Qārin, and affairs have an end."

Abū Jaʿfar read it in the genitive (bi-al-jarr) as an attribute of "amr", so it is conjoined to "the Hour", meaning: "and [the Hour] has drawn near. Every matter that is settled", meaning established, which is the truth, i.e., the manifestation [of truth] and its stability have drawn near, and this cannot occur except after the concealment of falsehood and its passing away has already taken place.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 4:

When He had warned and given good tidings, He said, informing that He encompasses knowledge of their affair from before the response, up to the splitting of the moon, and that He did not split it out of hope for their faith, but rather to make known their abandonment (by God), emphasizing for whoever hopes in them that the repeated succession of signs may perhaps necessitate for them assent (tasdiq), which implies that what came to them has no sufficiency: ﴿And there had certainly come to them﴾ of the kind of the splitting ﴿of the news﴾, i.e., the great, visible and audible matters, which by their greatness deserve that one inform of them with a great informing, especially what came in the Qur'an of the detailed explanation of the roots of the religion (usul al-din) and its branches (furu') and the reports of the former and the latter peoples, and the first and the last (worlds) ﴿wherein is⁠﴾ alone ﴿a deterrent (muzdajar)﴾, i.e., a place of restraint, which by its nature should cause them a great restraint from the falsehood it contains. But only those whom God willed were restrained from among them. Al-Qushayri said: Because God has drawn veils of ignorance over their sights, so they became blind to the places of right guidance.

Since what is in it (that content) may not be firm, he clarified it by His saying: ﴿Wisdom﴾ great, ﴿far-reaching﴾; that is, it has the greatest attainment of reaching the furthest ends of wisdom, owing to its soundness, its purity, and its clarity. Thus, along with its admonition, it contains encouragement, exhortations, rulings, and subtleties that are too great to be described. And since their being restrained follows from it, He made the following statement a consequence of that: ﴿So what good are the warnings﴾ — either as a clear negation, or as a reproachful, denunciatory interrogative — ﴿the warnings﴾: the warnings, the warners, and the matters warned of. What is actually meant by this is God Most High: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. Perhaps the indication in dropping the yā' of ﴿tughni﴾ (تُغْنِ), by the consensus of the mushaf codices, without any requirement in the wording, is that just as the final letter of the word was dropped, so too the fruit of warning was dropped, which is acceptance.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 6:**

Since the Prophet (ﷺ) was intensely eager for their salvation, he sometimes wished to grant them their demands, so as a result God said: ﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning: force yourself to turn away from that, for your duty is only to deliver the message, and guidance belongs to God alone. Having shown that the Hour draws near by granting some of their demands, which stand in its place in all respects because they indicate His power over them, and having followed this with a weaning from seeking any answer concerning the Hour, since such demands avail nothing, the noble souls longed to know the description of the Hour. So He answered this as a fresh statement (istinaf, a resumptive sentence) by mentioning its time and mentioning . . . the terrors that occur in it. He said, making it dependent on an implied clause, meaning: the Hour will certainly come with extreme nearness: ﴿The Day the Caller calls﴾. It is permissible, and God knows best, that the governing word of this phrase is ﴿turn away﴾ (Q. 27:28), because when they turned away at the time He called them, their recompense was that He would turn away from them on the day they needed Him, since recompense is of the same kind as the deed. So it is as if it were said, after He had counted the Resurrection as a certain matter about which there is no dispute: Turn away from them on that grievous day in which you are the accepted intercessor... and leave them to its terrors and calamities, for the loser has become clear. Their turning away only harms them, because their turning away from you does not harm you at all, whereas your turning away from them harms them with a harm beyond which there is no other harm, and God knows best.

The omission of the waw in ﴿يَدْعُ﴾ (yad'u, "calls") follows the orthography (rasm, the written form of the Mushaf) by the consensus of the codices, without any compelling reason, since the context is to show its nearness. It is as if this indicates that it will come at the mere sound of a call. Also, in omitting it there is a resemblance of the report to a command, indicating that this calling must be in the most magnificent, most perfect, most awesome and most powerful manner, just as every command issued by an obeyed authority is. Stopping on this and similar words without the waw is, for all the readers, in agreement with the orthography. This is because the principle is that whatever has a transmitted reading (riwayah) is followed even if it contradicts the orthography or the original form, while whatever has no transmitted reading from any of them is followed according to the orthography even if it contradicts the original form, since elision is attested in the speech of the Arabs, as in al-Wali and al-Muta'al among His Beautiful Names. However, the master of readings, Shams al-Din al-Jazari, said in his book entitled an-Nashr (The Diffusion) concerning these four letters: "This, and ﴿and man calls [for evil]﴾ (Q. 17:11) in Subhan, and ﴿God erases falsehood﴾ (Q. 42:24) in Shura, and ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ (Q. 96:18) in al-'Alaq: Abu 'Amr al-Dani explicitly reported from Ya'qub that they are stopped on with the waw, following the original form." Then he said: "I say: this is one of his unique transmissions, and I have recited it through his route, ﴿the Caller﴾," meaning: the blowing of the Trumpet, ﴿to a thing hideous﴾, of great strangeness in its being disliked, by which souls recoil and hearts are struck with dread, because nothing in it is anything but a departure from what preceded it of custom.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 7:

When he had explained his supplication by what made his affair terrifying, he explained the condition of those being called, for added dread, and said: ﴿With their eyes downcast﴾, that is, they look with the glance of one who is humbled, abased, of lowest rank, and overcome with desolation, which is the worst of conditions. He attributed the humbling (khushu') to the eyes because honor and humiliation become apparent in the glance, for humiliation is that its bearer casts it toward the ground, for example, together with a bearing by which that is recognized, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Humbled, they look out from the corner of their eyes, abased by humiliation﴾ [al-Shura: 45]. Its singular form (khashi'atan) in the reading of Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i indicates that the humbling has reached the utmost degree of intensity, and that it is attributed to every gaze equally. It is plural in the reading of the rest (khushsha'an), in the dialect of "akalūnī al-baraghīth" (the fleas ate me), with a dammah on the kha' and a shaddah on the shin, fathah-marked, or referring back to those being called. The eyes also indicate, to some degree, that all of this is distributed across the eyes.

When he had explained, in this manner, of their condition what indicates the horror of that day, he explained the manner of their coming out, as a clarification of what necessarily follows from imagining it, namely increased terror, and said: ﴿They will come out﴾, that is, in a continuous succession, the most noble first and then the next, ﴿from the graves﴾, that is, the tombs prepared for hearing the blast of the Trumpet, ﴿as if they﴾ in their multitude and the piling of some of them upon others, of their great and small, weak and strong, ﴿were locusts dispersed﴾, that is, scattered, spread out, bewildered, submitting to whoever disperses them, after having been in a stillness mixed with one another, having in reality no direction that they would aim at if left to themselves.

Since dispersing (al-intishar) can sometimes be a sign of ease and dignity, He said, clarifying that the matter is contrary to that, as an increase in the terror of that Day and a confirmation of what preceded of its description: ﴿Hastening toward the summoner﴾, that is: rushing, fearful, coming forward with their gazes fixed upon him, not turning away from him, stretching out their necks toward him, lifting their heads straight ahead, not looking to anything else, as one does who looks in humiliation, submission, silence and abjection.

When He had described the state of all of them, He restricted the state of the falsifiers, so He said: ﴿Says﴾, that is, by way of repetition: ﴿the disbelievers﴾, that is, those who in the world were deeply engaged in concealing the proofs and displaying the misleading falsehoods: ﴿This﴾, that is, the time in which we are now, with the terrors we see, ﴿is a difficult day﴾, that is, in the utmost degree of difficulty, hardship and severity, and that is according to their state on it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 9:

When His command, glorified is He, to His Prophet ﷺ to turn away from them had preceded, as a threat to them, and He had made clear what He intended regarding the matter of the Hour (al-sa'ah), because the previous mention of it had called for that, and because it is the greatest terror with which they are threatened, and as an explanation that creation was created only for its sake, since it is the focal point of wisdom (mahatt al-hikmah), and He concluded with its difficulty upon the disbelievers, He completed that threat with the punishment of this world as a deterrent to the people of harshness (ghiladhah) who are restricted to the perceptible (al-mahsusat), so He mentioned the difficulty of a day that was upon the disbelievers in it. He said, threatening Quraysh by making the story an example for them regarding their destruction and regarding the matter of the Hour, in that just as He destroyed the people of the earth in a single instant by the water He sent down, He is capable of destroying them in a single instant by the Cry (al-sayhah); and just as He directed this direction which [what] had not been heard of its like in destruction, He is capable of directing it in revival at the Resurrection in a manner the like of which is not known, wherein bodies will sprout and servants will live, as a reply to one who was as if he had said: "This is what they are promised after death, so is there for them a punishment before it that indicates complete power?" ﴿Kadhdhabat﴾, that is: they committed the great denial by which they generalized it to all the messages and all the messengers, and He made their act feminine to belittle them and to diminish their affair in comparison with His power.

When what they had of resolve upon it and determination not to disengage from it, because it was a disposition (jibillah) encompassing all the time after them, and they had established the practice of denial, so upon them, along with their own burden, was the burden of whoever came after them, and the time before them was small in comparison with what came after it in nonexistence, therefore He mentioned the adverb of time without a preposition [of genitive], because although it is the truth, it is greater in consolation, so He said: ﴿before them﴾, that is: in all the time that has passed, some of it by actuality and some of it by potentiality due to the strength of resolve: ﴿the people of Noah﴾, despite what they had of strength and what they had of spread (intishar) in all the regions.

When He mentioned their denial as an indication that it was a disposition for them, by which they wholly denied prophethood, so they had no share in affirming the truth, and their condition does not differ in relation to anyone among the people, whoever he might be, therefore He made this absolute the cause of His saying: ﴿So they denied Our servant﴾, that is: despite his greatness in relation to Us, because he never worshipped other than Us, together with Our honouring him with messengership, so their denial was a branch of what entered into their absolute denial that encompasses everything that can be denied, and it is a ruin (mayd). ﴿And they said﴾ along with the denial also, in addition to concealing what had appeared from him of guidance: ﴿Mad⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ (majnun)﴾, that is: so this one, to whom appear extraordinary things from the matter of the jinn.

When raising the voice against the Prophet is, whoever he might be, exceedingly ugly and extremely harsh, how much more so if he is a messenger, how much more so if he is among the Ulu al-'Azm, how much more so if it is in the form of denial against him, how much more so if it is in the form of what is done by one who has no standing in any way, He said, building the verb for the unknown (passive), indicating its foulness without regard to a speaker, and as a notice that this did not come only from their elders but from their great and their small: ﴿And he was rebuked (wazdujira)﴾, that is: they exerted themselves in his reproach, his threatening and his intimidation, and this spread among all of them with the utmost harshness, as a restraint upon him from the message and a prevention of him from it. The meaning is that they said: he has gained the upper hand over them through madness.

When this continued long among them, and their generations passed over it, generation after generation, until more of the time of warning had elapsed for him than had elapsed for the community of this final Prophet until our present day, and Allah informed him that none of them would believe except those who had already believed with him, (p-104) this resulted in his supplication for relief from them. Therefore He said, turning the address toward the attributes of beneficence, lordship and bounty, as an indication that He answered his supplication and responded to his call: ﴿So he called upon his Lord﴾, that is, the One who nurtured him with beneficence toward him through his messengership, informing Him that, having despaired of their answering: ﴿that I am overcome﴾, that is, by my entire people, through force and strength, not through proof. He emphasized it because whoever turns away from the Greatest King is a likely object of victory. It also serves as an intensified complaint and a display of the humiliation of servitude, for Allah, glorified is He, knows the secret and the open of His servant, so supplication was legislated in its essence only to manifest humility, and likewise the emphasis within it. ﴿So help [me]﴾, that is, bring about My victory over them, You alone, in the most emphatic manner.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 11:

When He (glory be to Him) responded to him, He made His saying, returning to the manifestation of majesty, a consequence of his supplication, to inform of an increase in the anger which necessarily always entails comprehensiveness in punishment: ﴿So We opened﴾, meaning, as a consequence of his supplication [that We opened] an opening befitting Our majesty ﴿the gates of the heaven﴾, all of them, in all directions. He expressed the plurality (jam' al-qilla, the plural of paucity) with the sense of abundance, because it is the custom of the Arabs to use it metaphorically for that, and it is more elegant and more well known than "bibān" (another word for gates). The context of majesty refuses that it be for anything else. And since the intent is to magnify the matter of the water by mentioning its condition in which it was, so that it is as if the one relating it witnessed it, it was made as if it were a sign by which the heaven was opened, so He said: ﴿with water pouring forth﴾, meaning poured out in the most eloquent manner of flowing and pouring, in greatness and abundance. For this reason He did not say "with rain (maṭar)", because it departs from that customary (sense). And that continued for forty days.

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾. That is, We split it open by what We possess of greatness, and We cleaved, sent forth and dispatched [the water]; ﴿the earth [became] springs﴾, that is, all the springs of the earth. But He deviated from this expression (p-105) for the sake of awe-inspiring effect, first by vagueness and then by clarification, and to convey that the surface of the earth had become entirely springs.

Since al-ma' (water) is a noun of genus (ism jins) which applies to its various kinds just as it applies to a single kind, and since He had mentioned the water of the sky and the water of the earth, He made the following statement a consequence of that: ﴿So the waters met﴾, that is, the known waters, namely the water of the sky and the water of the earth, by reason of this Our act. He increased their magnitude further with the particle of elevation (isti'la'), saying: ﴿for a matter [already] decreed﴾. Since this greatness was established for this event, it might be supposed that it had occurred haphazardly and exceeded the limit commanded; He therefore indicated that, in relation to His greatness, it is of utmost insignificance, saying: ﴿that had been decreed﴾, that is: although it was within His power at every time with the utmost ease, its decree had already taken place from eternity, so that it could not exceed that by a single drop or more, nor destroy anyone other than those We commanded Him to destroy. By the use of the lightening form (al-takhfif) He indicated the utmost ease of that, glorified is He.

When he (al-Biqa'i) had mentioned what was known from him by means of what he mentioned of his breaking of custom, and that his answering of his supplication, upon him be prayers and peace, he mentioned the completion of the victory through his deliverance, so he said: ﴿And We carried him﴾, i.e., by what We have of might, upon the back of that water after the whole face of the earth had become one course. He omitted the qualified noun to magnify it, urging one to recognize it by reflecting on the speech, so he said: ﴿upon one of planks and nails﴾, i.e., a ship possessing ﴿planks﴾, meaning pieces of wood that were sawn until they became broad, ﴿and nails﴾, plural of dissar (nail), which is what the ship is fastened with, and by which its planks are joined, and some of them are fitted into others with a nail of iron, wood, or fibers of palm, in a manner of massiveness, strength, propulsion and firmness. Perhaps he (God) expressed the ship by what explains it, as an alert to His power over what He wills of unstitching the sewn and sewing the unstitched, such that that made thing becomes, by what He prepared it for, to be intended from it, even if that intended purpose is great and that made thing is great.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 14:

Since that was a departure from custom, it was possible that there would be another departure from custom in the ship, namely its remaining still on the surface of the water without movement. So he made clear that the matter is not so, and said, manifesting another departure from custom in its course: ﴿It runs﴾, that is, the ship ﴿under Our eyes﴾, that is, kept safe from entering the sea of darkness, or from any other calamities befalling it, by Our guarding it with the greatness We possess, the guarding of one who looks at a thing repeatedly and never turns away from it at all. Some also allowed that it may be a broken plural (ʿuyūn) of the word for a spring of water (ʿayn). Then he gave the reason for that with His words: ﴿A recompense﴾, that is, for Our servant Noah, peace be upon him. However, he expressed it here in a way that conveys the cause, so that the listener would beware of the same punishment befalling him should he commit the same deeds as his people. So He said: ﴿for him who had been disbelieved﴾, and He expressed the long duration of their disbelief [by His words]: ﴿kāna kufira﴾, that is, disbelief was committed against him, and he is the most sublime of blessings. So He said, "upon the people of that time," and that is the recompense of whoever denies blessings. It is also permissible that what is meant by it is his people, and it makes clear that disbelief came from them in such a manner that they seemed to be created upon it, to the extent that it seemed to have been done to them, in agreement with the reading of Mujahid with the active voice (lil-fa'il).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 15:

When the report of his deliverance by being carried in it had been completed, he drew attention to its traces with His saying: ﴿And We have left it as a sign﴾, that is, this great act of the ship's sailing in this manner and the preservation of its kind, indicating what We possess of greatness. It was said: that same ship (p-107) remained on al-Judi until this community reached its remnants, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a great mark of what We possess of all-encompassing knowledge and complete power. ﴿So is there any who will take heed?﴾, that is, one who strives in admonition because of this matter, for what is due from the created beings of gratitude to the Creator, through what His messengers guided to, as they said.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 16:

When the Exalted had first mentioned His saying: ﴿So what good were warnings?﴾ [al-Qamar: 5], and followed it with the mention of His destruction of those who denied, and the matter of those people was of such majesty and greatness that it is fitting for the listener to ask about it and to learn their circumstances, so that he may be guided by them, He followed this with His saying, as a consequence of the reminder, in the form of a question of denunciation and reproach: ﴿Then how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ That is, how did it come about and become real (wujida wa-tahaqqaqa) — ﴿My punishment﴾ upon those who denied, disbelieved, and denied My messengers, and ﴿My warnings﴾, that is, the warnings issued by Me and the warners who conveyed from Me. For He saved Noah, peace be upon him, and those who believed with him from among his descendants and others, and granted them enjoyment after destroying their enemy, and made all people now his offspring.

Al-Qushayri said: In this there is strength for the hope of the people of religion: when they encounter a trial in the religion of Allah and others deny what Allah has given them, Allah will soon destroy their enemy, enable them over their homes and lands, and cause them to inherit what was theirs. Such is the custom of Allah with all people of misguidance. — End quote.

The meaning of repeating this to them, after the reminder of the stories of these nations which We brought them, made easy for the understanding of their young and old, their males and females, is: how was My seizing of them, and what was the outcome of My warning them, so that they may take heed, and the warning of the warners may benefit them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 17:

Since this detailed account was among the things revealed at the beginning of the Qur'an as facilitation for the community, he drew attention to that by His saying: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾, meaning, according to His greatness (p-108) ﴿the Qur'an﴾, meaning, according to what it has of gathering and distinguishing and the greatness appropriate to its being a attribute of Ours, ﴿for remembrance﴾, meaning admonition, recollection, reflection, understanding, memorization, and honouring for whoever observes it. Ibn Burjan said: "We sent it down in the Arabic tongue, and sent it down to the understandings, gradually. We addressed them in their customs, informed them of their deeds before they were done, gave them knowledge and certainty before their own essences, struck examples for them, and lengthened for them in these deeds so that they might remember the covenant taken from them." Al-Qushayri said: "He made its recitation easy upon the tongues of one people, its knowledge easy upon the hearts of another people, its understanding easy upon the hearts of another people, and its memorization easy upon the hearts of another people, and they are all the People of the Qur'an, all of them are the People of God and His elite." End of quotation. The verse, by way of conjunction and meaning, refers back to ﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news﴾ [al-Qamar: 4] and the verses following it. The meaning is: Were We, with the greatness We possess, to wish, We would have brought them expressions whose fragrance they could not smell, and eloquences whose meaning they could not find the way to at all. But We did not do that; rather We addressed them with something more eloquent than their own eloquence, together with facilitating the understanding of what We addressed them with. So in that there are two inimitabilities: the first is that it is above their eloquence, and the second is that, despite its loftiness, the intelligent and the dull share in the basic understanding of it.

Since this Great Qur'an gathers the translation of His deeds, glory be to Him, in this existence, the witnessed and the unseen, which He informed us of, and an explanation of what He sent down to us of His Most Beautiful Names and His Highest Attributes by which He made Himself known to us; and since He, glory be to Him, made the creation of the human being comprehensive, there is not any of His deeds except that in the human self there is a manifest trace of it, looking toward reflection on the Qur'an and recognition of its secrets through the reminder which occurs... since the human being knew it, then forgot it, until he no longer is able to summon it by himself; so when he is reminded of it, he remembers it. Thus He said, drawing attention to the great effect of knowledge and of the Qur'an, which is its path, by repetition (p-109) and by expression with what is of the root of remembrance, as it is the thing preserved for the human being through what He prepared for him of facilitation of his matter: ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ Al-Bukhari said at the end of his Sahih: Matar al-Warraq said: "Is there any seeker of knowledge who will be helped in it?" This admonition has been repeated in this surah four times, and the last sentence of it has been mentioned, separated from the facilitation of the Qur'an, twice: once at the beginning of the stories, which is the story of Noah, peace be upon him, and once as it comes at its end, following the story of Pharaoh, which is His saying: "Then how was My punishment and warning?" The same, and "Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?" was repeated in al-Rahman thirty-one times. I reflected on the secret of that, and it became clear to me, and God is the Guide, that what precedes this surah in the Mufassal is four surahs, of which this surah is the last. So reference was made to remembrance with each of them, urging reflection upon them, by a verse whose words end with a word whose letters recur in the five surahs, and one of its letters is assimilated into another after each of the two has been changed. So this word, whose meaning is remembrance, indicated the five outward senses, which are the beginnings of knowledge. What was at the beginning and end of these admonitions, because it is empty of mention of the Qur'an, corresponded to the two letters whose extremities are for weakness through expression and transposition. But since the two letters, by assimilation, are like one letter, the two sentences corresponding to them are like one verse among those four. This first and last was indicated as referring to this surah, which gathered the reminder of the four surahs, and was emptied of mention of the facilitation of the Qur'an, because the surahs open with erasure and what is close to erasure, which is the verse of the night, and facilitation in it, and the Hour, which is the most hidden of the unseen; and everyone in it other than God is erased, to strip the whole matter from them. The first and the last were singled out for it (p-110) because of a common link between them: the drowning of the staff in the water, the salvation of the obedient, some by the ark and some by the very sea which is the course of ships. The admonition in which the Qur'an is mentioned at the end of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, although it is general to all the Qur'an, was an allusion to the specific reminder of surah Qaf, because of the comprehensive encompassing link between them: the encompassing of the mountain of Qaf over the whole earth, and the flood of Noah's people over the entirety of the earth. The verse in the story of 'Ad refers to surah al-Dhariyat, because both were by wind. The verse in the story of Thamud refers to the reminder by al-Tur, through the common link between them of shaking, quaking, humiliation and thunderbolt. As for the story of Thamud, it is manifest; and as for al-Tur, it is because of its crushing and the thunderbolt that struck the Children of Israel there, and thunderbolt is mentioned at the end of al-Tur. What is in the story of Lot refers to al-Najm, because their cities were raised up to the clouds of the sky, then overturned and followed by stones. So since the matter was thus, and since the blessings encompass the human being from his six directions, the five senses were multiplied by the six directions, and they became thirty, as if it were said: "Is there any reminder with this Qur'an," especially what preceded this surah of it in the Mufassal, of the blessings God has upon him in himself and in the horizons. The first part of them is indicated by a reminder, and the second by repeating the mention of the favours; so every verse is a repetition, ending at the specified number and at the totality by the totality, so that it may be known that God's blessings encompass him in a manner that no one can accomplish except God, to whom belongs the encompassing of all the attributes of perfection, the greatest of which, from the standpoint of its being the foundation upon which everything is built, is the Oneness, free from partnership. So one fears, from disobedience to Him, that He would strip him of His blessings or one of them, and he would find no one who could sustain them or any of them besides Him, (p-111) or punish him with something like the punishment of these nations, or with other than that, of what He has of the encompassing of power and knowledge, so he would find no one who could turn away from him any of it, glory be to Him. As for the single extra one, it is an indication that the basis of that perception is the intellect and the senses, just as the purpose of all of that is one, which is God, exalted. All of these things are means to knowing Him. Also, the one is an indication that the increase of the blessings is from the bounty of God, exalted, which does not cease, just as the One, which is the root of number, never ceases. So whenever its increase is sufficient, a cycle begins, then another cycle begins, forever and ever. There is another very wondrous point to the repetition: it is the emphasis of the affirmation, indicating the intensification of anger, which demands the utmost punishment. Just as one whose anger is intensified by a person's denial of something of his killing, when he has made it clear to him in the utmost clarity by various matters, while he rebels and is most contentious, he seizes him and gathers him in a gathering from which he cannot turn away from the truth in their presence, and he submits while he is in his grip; so he mentions those meanings among that gathering, and whenever he mentions to him a kind of them in their presence, he says: "Has this become clear to you?" That denier says: "Yes, it has become clear to me." This only increases him in anger because of his earlier great anger and contentiousness. So he mentions to him another meaning, then says: "Has this become clear to you?" He says: "Yes, by God." He does not pay attention to his admission of that, and mentions to him another kind, saying the like, desiring to increase his rebuke and his shaming. And so on until he is satisfied with all of that, as a warning to his contentiousness and to the sufficiency of each kind of them for what is intended from him of clarification. Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: "Its benefit is that they renew, upon hearing each report of the reports of the former peoples, remembrance and admonition, and that they begin again with alertness and awakening when they hear the urging towards it and the rousing to all of that, and that the staves be struck for them many times, and the bell be rung for them repeatedly, lest heedlessness overcome them and the rule of unawareness take hold of them. Such is the rule of the repetitions, so that the lessons may be present to the hearts, pictured to the minds, mentioned and not forgotten in due time." End of quotation. For something like what has passed, or close to it, He repeated the threat of punishment six times: four of them are: "Then how was My punishment and warning?" and two of them: "Taste My punishment and warning." These two are in the same position as one of the four, so that the six return to the five which indicates them, ﴿mudhakir﴾ being an indication that just as the five senses were multiplied in the six directions for the sake of the blessings, which are the bringing of benefits, they were multiplied in them for the sake of reminding of the removal of vengeances, which is the warding off of corruptions and the warning against them. Among the benefits of the repetition of the six, which return to the five, twice: once for bringing blessings, and another for warding off vengeances, is that the senses are repeated outwardly and inwardly. Whoever submits his tongue to the Qur'an outwardly, his outward senses are sound, and his inward ones are illumined for him; and whoever refuses is punished through the inward ones, so the outward ones are corrupted. The number six was chosen for the two admonitions, with the intention of five to the group, because six is a complete number, since its fractional parts, when added together, make it complete, neither exceeding it nor falling short: they are the half, the third, and the sixth. This number is equal to the five pillars of Islam, and its enclosure is jihad, which is the pillar of the piety of the God-fearing, the people of the seat of truth, who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend of what We have provided them, and who believe in what has been sent down to their Prophet, peace be upon him, and what was sent down before him, which is alluded to by fasting: ﴿Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 183], and by pilgrimage: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for the people and a sanctuary﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125], and by jihad: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], up to His saying: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, while it is hateful to you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216]. That is an indication that this religion is complete, with no addition in it and no deficiency, because the Prophet who was sent is the seal of the prophets and the completion of the chosen messengers.

Since the people of 'Ad had become arrogant through their strength and power, and the condition of Quraysh was close to that, by their saying that they were the most protected of the Arabs, the strongest of them, and the most gathered of them in perfections and the highest, He repeated that in their story twice, as an increase in the reminder and warning to Quraysh, especially since the beginning of their punishment was from their own land, Mecca the Honoured, as is explained in their story. He repeated the command to taste in the story of Lot, peace be upon him, because they were punished with what would deter anyone who had a heart with obliteration. When that did not benefit them, something greater than it came upon them, so they became like yesterday's past. So for each instance of punishment there is a command to taste. They were singled out for the command to taste because in their vile indecency there is what they find pleasurable. The punishment of these nations encompassed all directions: for the people of Noah and Lot, peace be upon them both, there was drowning by rainwater and stones of baked clay, and from the springing water and the sinking into the earth; and what is in the generality of their punishment of the covering of the remaining directions. God is the Guide.

Once the story of Nuh, peace be upon him, concluded with this tremendous catastrophe, it was bound to lead the listener to suppose that no one after them would fall short, even if no messenger were sent, so how much more so when one was sent. Thus he yearned to know what happened after them: did things turn out as he supposed, or did people revert to their (natural) dispositions? The story of 'Ad was the greatest story that occurred after the people of Nuh, peace be upon him, according to what the Arabs know, so it is fitting that it serve as an admonition to them. Their punishment was by the wind which destroyed them and uprooted their mountains, which had been in their places (p-114) of piled-up sand. Moving them to other places is the clearest proof that He, exalted is He, will set the mountains in motion on the Day of Judgment. Beyond this, in its extraordinary arrangement, there is the depiction of the blowing into the Trumpet, once for the Resurrection and once for the revival. He was therefore answered with His saying: ﴿'Ad denied﴾, that is, they brought about a general and absolute denial, which necessitated their denial of My messengers, Hud, peace be upon him, in his call to them to Me and his warning them of My punishment.

Since it is the custom of kings, or some of them, that when they destroy many people of their soldiers, some people like them who were saved by the same sins are raised up by them and won over so that their army is not destroyed and their rule is not disrupted, He followed the report of their denial with the announcement of their transgression, because He does not care about anything, since everything is in His grip. And since their denial occurred only by His will, just as His punishment is by His decree, He said, as a consequence of that: ﴿Then how﴾, that is, then, in light of these circumstances, because of their denial, ﴿was My punishment﴾ upon them ﴿and My warnings﴾, that is, My warning to them through the tongue of My messenger. He repeated this interrogative at the end of their story, so there were two (such statements) in their story, as was mentioned earlier concerning its secret. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 19:

When He mentioned their denial and followed it with their punishment, the listener knew that He is of tremendous majesty, so he was prompted to want to know Him; thus He resumed His speech, emphasizing, as a warning that the Quraysh's conduct in denying was like their conduct, as if they were denying their punishment: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a wind﴾ by Our majesty. He expressed it with the preposition of elevation (ʿalā), to indicate vengeance, saying: ﴿upon them a wind﴾. And since the wind may sometimes be seen directly, He described it with what indicates its state, saying: ﴿violent (ṣarṣaran)﴾, meaning: of intense cold and sound. And since the aim of the surah is to bring near the establishment of the Hour (al-Sāʿa) (p-115) and to describe their hastening toward the Caller with speed, it was fitting to express their punishment with the least possible, so He expressed it with "a day," which is intended as a generic noun encompassing the little and the much. It may be used to express a measure of time in which a clear matter is completed, whether it be a moment, or days, or months, or much of that, or less, like the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Badr, and the Day of Death, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To your Lord on that Day is the driving﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 30]: ﴿on a day﴾. He emphasized its evil by censuring its time, saying: ﴿ill-omened (naḥs)﴾, meaning: of intense ugliness. It is said that it was a Wednesday at the end of the month, which was Shawwal, eight days remaining until the setting of Wednesday. He verified it, because the intended "day" is the genus, not a single day, by the description, saying: ﴿continuous (mustamirr)﴾, meaning: strong in its ill-omen, effective, carrying out what it was commanded of that, intense in its causes, its bitterness existing in a manner desired by its Sender at every time, its bitterness firmly established, strong and enduring until the time of the execution of the intended purpose.

When its description in itself was known, he followed it with its description in terms of what is done to it, and said: ﴿It uproots﴾, i.e., it takes some of them from the surface of the earth and some from pits they dug to protect themselves from the punishment. He made explicit the place of the pronoun (al-idmar, the use of a pronoun in place of a noun) so that the statement would be clear and cover both males and females. He expressed it with a word derived from swaying (al-naws), as a favor to them, and said: ﴿the people﴾, who are mere forms with no steadiness through the spirits of piety. So it sends them flying between the heaven and the earth as if they were scattered dust (al-habaʾ al-manthur), and it cuts off their heads from their bodies and changes their colors to black, blackening them. For this reason he said: ﴿as if they were﴾, i.e., when they are uprooted and cast down with no spirits in them, as if they were ﴿trunks﴾, i.e., the roots of ﴿palm trees﴾ whose tops have been cut off. Since the judgment here is upon their outward state, and the outward is less than the inward, he kept the wording to the literal sense with his saying ﴿uprooted﴾ (p-116), i.e., broken and felled from the bottom of its hollow and the root of its planting. The comparison points to their being tall while their heads have been cut off. In al-Haqqah the comparison was made with the inward part, in which lie the principal organs and the subtle meanings, so he made the adjective feminine, taking into account the sense of "palm tree" and not the subtlety of the... (the text here reads: "لِلُطْفِها") — and God knows best.

Now that what He had told them of their punishment matched what had terrified them at the outset, He confirmed this, in light of what had preceded of its secret. So He said, as a consequence of it, indicating that because of the severity of its terror it is something one must ask about: ﴿Then how was My punishment﴾, O questioner, and He turned the speech to the first person as a reminder to the servants to guard the station of Tawhid. ﴿...and My warnings?﴾ That is, My admonition, or My messengers in their warning: did it come true?

When He, glory be to Him, had completed His warning against the likes of their condition, by an admonition that had considered the full arrangement of what is in Surat al-Dhariyat, He followed that with an alert that the listener should expect an exhortation to that. He said, emphasizing against what most listeners held of denial, whether in word or in state, informing that He had made easy the path of escape from such great trials to Himself, and made reliance upon Him sound. He returned to the manifestation of greatness, as a notice that the facilitation of the Qur'an for what has been mentioned of its inimitability can only be by a greatness that exceeds the powers of humankind and is beyond the capacity of power. ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy﴾, according to what We possess of greatness in the Essence and the Attributes, ﴿the Qur'an﴾, which gathers and distinguishes all of it, and what this story indicates of its divisions, ﴿for remembrance﴾, for memorization, for honor, for understanding, for contemplation, for admonition, and for being admonished, in what We have variously expressed of kinds of admonition, together with an alert to memorization through brevity, sweetness of expression, nearness of understanding, sublimity of meanings, firmness of composition, variety of arts, multiplicity of branches, and soundness of connection. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ That is: as a consequence of this great matter which We have done, it is the place for asking about the states of the listeners: Is there among them anyone who devotes himself to memorizing it, then to reflecting upon it and understanding it, and who takes admonition from what befell the earlier nations, and who recalls all that has been variously expressed of sayings, and applies them to himself and their conditions, and makes that for Our countenance, so that he casts upon it, through Our honoring him with it, the matter of his worldly life and his hereafter.

[p. 117]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 23:

When this was the place for turning attention to reflecting on the admonitions of the Qur'an, and Thamud was the greatest admonition after 'Ad, because of their Cry (sayha), which broke the covenants, depicting the Hour with its two blasts (nafkhatayn), the one that causes death and then the one that brings back to life, and He said, making their verb feminine, indicating the lowliness of their aspirations and the lowliness of their deeds, informing that whoever denies is destroyed, by way of answering someone who might say, expressing astonishment at denial after what had happened in the two previous stories of punishment: ﴿Thamud denied﴾, that is, the people of Salih, ﴿the warnings﴾, the warnings and all the warners, because they constituted one single sharia. Then he gave the reason for that and followed it, informing by the pronoun that those who directly committed this disbelief were their men, lest it be thought that they were women only:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 24:

﴿Then they said﴾, denying in the utmost degree what had come to them from God: ﴿"Is it a mere mortal﴾, a denial of the prophethood of this kind, so that the denial of prophethood [i.e., denial] of their own prophet would be in the most eloquent and greatest manner, and they made the denial greater by their saying, putting first the absence of distinction from them, given his particularity: ﴿"from among us"﴾, that is, he has no superiority over us, so what is the basis for his being singled out for this from among us? They increased this [emphasis] by saying: ﴿"alone"﴾, that is, there is no one with him to support him. Then he explained the verb governing "a mortal" by his saying: ﴿"that we should follow him"﴾, that is, we would strive against ourselves in casting off what we are accustomed to and the ways of our fathers, and in confessing against ourselves the feebleness of reason and the antiquity of ignorance, while we are [more] numerous, stronger, and more perceptive and discerning than people. Then they drew a conclusion from this severe denial, saying, emphasizing the sense that their own speech deserves to be disbelieved: ﴿"Indeed we would then be"﴾, that is, if we follow him, ﴿"in error"﴾, that is, departure from the right course surrounding us, ﴿"and madness"﴾, that is, our end in that error would be to fall into the beginnings of a matter whose outcome we do not know, for it has not been tested or examined, and no one before us has gone ahead to be a precedent for us, so that this would drag us into madness, hunger and fire, as happens to those who go to it in deserts, in kinds of heat, with the blazing heat of mountains, the heat of error, and the heat of worries and fears, and that is from the fire with which we have been threatened. This is the meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's (may Allah be pleased with them both) interpretation of it as "punishment." Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna took it as the plural of "sa'ir" (blaze). The meaning is: indeed we would be, if we follow you as you say, combining error and punishment in all its kinds.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 25:

When what they said contained the greatest denial, the soundness of which was indicated in their assumption by what they hinted at, namely that he is a human being like them, and yet he is one individual among them, so he is not the most excellent of them, and he is alone, so his thinking has not been strengthened by the thinking of others so as to be a source of trust, they pointed to him with another matter, which they also presented in the manner of denial, and they hinted by the word "cast down" that in his haste it was as if he had fallen from a height. So they said: ﴿Has the Reminder been cast upon him﴾, i.e., sent down suddenly and swiftly, because among them he was not in the arena of this affair, and they had not conferred about it before he brought it, nor had anything of it reached them; rather he brought it to them suddenly, with the utmost haste. And since "casting" usually applies to bodies, it was more appropriate, to dispel this illusion, to place the deputy of the agent first, unlike what preceded in Sad. So they said: ﴿the Reminder﴾, i.e., the revelation through which the greatest honour comes. They used the preposition ﴿upon﴾ to indicate that such a thing as he claimed is only said to be from a dominant decree and an overpowering command, so he said: ﴿upon him﴾. They indicated the aspect of wonder and denial by the restriction in their words: ﴿from among us﴾, i.e., while among us there is one more fitting for this in age, nobility and honour.

Since this interrogation, being a denial, carries the meaning of negation, they turned away from it with their words, in the manner of a conclusion, as a continuation of what the interrogation implied, such as: the matter is not as he claims: ﴿Nay, he is﴾, because of the doubts we have presented, ﴿a liar﴾, i.e., exceedingly lying, ﴿insolent﴾, i.e., boastful, whom idleness has overcome, so that his self has pleased him with arrogance, tyranny and insolence, and he has become energetic in that until he has become like a saw which is free for cutting and prepared for it, rough in matter, bad in character and effect; so he wants to exalt himself.
