Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 26:

When this was the utmost of censure for those who deserve the utmost of praise, Allah the Exalted answered it as an admonition to His servants, so that they would not say what they know to be false, or say what they do not know to be true, with His words: ﴿They will know﴾ by a promise that admits no failure. Since the intended meaning is nearness, because it is more effective in warning, He said: ﴿tomorrow﴾, that is, in the coming near time, because everything whose coming is certain is near, at the descent of punishment in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. The reading of Ibn 'Amir, Hamza, and Ruways from Ya'qub with the second person (khitab) is an iltifat (shift of grammatical person) that indicates the utmost anger: ﴿Who is the liar, the insolent?﴾ That is, the lying and the insolence, which is the belittling of people and arrogance toward the truth they have brought, is specific to them and restricted to them. It does not extend beyond them to those it aims at, because they made lying their habit, and it did not go beyond them so that anything of it would be claimed for Salih (peace be upon him). Thus the speech specifies them in lying and confines it to them by its context in this ambiguous yet fair manner, which contains a awe for the heart and a stirring of the soul that no one knows in its true extent except Allah the Exalted. And the more naturally sound a person's disposition and the greater his knowledge, the greater his appreciation of it.

When this became clear from what precedes it, that He, glory be to Him, had decided the matter between them, the listener's curiosity was aroused to know the outcome. So God, exalted is He, said, beginning a new statement and indicating that they had demanded from him a sign confirming his truthfulness: ﴿Indeed, We﴾, that is, with the majesty that belongs to Us, ﴿are sending the she-camel﴾, that is, bringing it into existence and bringing it out, just as they proposed. It came from a rock which We made fit for that purpose and singled out from among the rocks, as a proof of Our sending Salih (peace be upon him), specifying it for him from among his people. The reason was that they said to Salih (peace be upon him): "We want to know who among us is in the right, by calling upon our gods and having you call upon your God. Whoever's god answers him, we will know that he is in the right." So they called upon their idols, but these did not answer them. They said, "Now you call upon Him." He said, "What do you want?" They said, "Bring forth for us from this rock a she-camel, heavy with young, that is ten months pregnant." He agreed to this on condition of their faith, and they promised him that and confirmed it, but they lied after they had lied about their gods answering them. He, (ﷺ), was truthful in everything he said, so his Lord, glory be to Him, informed him that He would answer them by bringing it out. ﴿As a trial for them﴾, that is, a test by which He mixes with them, so that He turns them away from the state in which they had promised to be, and answers them concerning it. God, glory be to Him, made the following consequence of that the command to him to wait and watch what they would do after it came out, because of what the consequences of the trial would bring them to. So He said: ﴿So watch them﴾, that is, burden yourself with waiting for them regarding what will become their recompense for their deeds, waiting as one who guards them, while He is the All-Knowing, the Ever-Knowing, for they will surely arrive through their deeds at the calamity called Umm al-ʿUrqub (the "mother of the nape", a figure of a calamity that wraps around the neck like a noose on a person's neck), so that they will be like one upon whose neck something has been placed. The form of the verb in the reflexive measure (iftaʿala) indicates that he will suffer from it a severe harm before the dispute is resolved. So He said: ﴿and be patient﴾, that is, exert yourself and strive to be patient with them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 28:

﴿And inform them﴾ means: tell them with a great telling of a great matter, namely that the water they drink, which is the water of their well, ﴿that the water is a shared allotment between them﴾, that is, between Thamud and the she-camel. The pronoun used for it is that of rational beings (ḍamīr man ya'qil), by way of predominance. That is, when we send her forth, there is a day on which they have no share in the water, and a day on which she leaves not a single drop in the well for any of them to take. She widens everything for them in place of water with milk. When He had informed them of the distribution of the water, He made known, by way of a resumptive statement (isti'nāf) that it was in a strange manner, saying: ﴿every draught﴾, that is, of that and its portion and its watering place at the time it is drunk, ﴿shall be attended﴾, that is, deserving, because of the wondrous matter in it, that those present should attend it with great attendance, and that they should exert themselves for it, because in its abundance and goodness it became like the water of the town for the desert dwellers, and it was fit that its attendants should contend for it because of its goodness, return to it, that many should gather at it, and accustom themselves to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 29:

Since the sense is: the matter was as We have described, the appointed period We set out continued, and they fell into trial [as] We have informed, ﴿So they called to their companion﴾ because of the trial, [namely] Qudar ibn Salif (Qudar ibn Salif), whom they appointed out of insolence and wickedness to slaughter the she-camel, and We were denied in it by their promise of faith and of honouring her with kindness, and he was the most wretched of the former ones; ﴿so he took it in hand﴾, meaning: he carried out, because of their calling, a seizing of the kind that no seizing is like, so he laid hold of what he had no right to lay hold of, by reason of the she-camel, namely his sword in his hand, standing firm in the matter that arose from this seizing in every case, and he raised his head with utmost resolve, stretched out his hands with a great stretching, raised them, and stood on the tips of his toes, when they urged him to it, that is: they asked him for it, and he complied with them, and took the she-camel with that sword, unconcerned and heedless. ﴿Then he hamstrung [her]﴾, meaning: there resulted from this great effort that he truly fulfilled what they had shown to be false in the promise of kindness towards her and insolence, namely the carrying out of the hamstringing, of which there was no hamstringing like it in that time, namely the hamstringing of the she-camel, which is the sign of Allah, and her destruction.

Now that their lying had reached this grave extreme, built upon utmost wickedness, Allah the Exalted confirmed the truth of His threat to them, on the supposition that this occurred. So He brought down His punishment upon them in a manner which, because of its magnitude, deserves to be inquired about. He, glory be to Him, drew attention to its greatness by presenting it in the interrogative form, as a consequence of the deed of the most wretched, saying: ﴿So how was My punishment﴾, and He preserved the station of Divine Oneness as had passed, saying: ﴿My punishment﴾. That is, it was in a state and manner that deserves that one strive to come to know it and to ask about it. ﴿And My warnings﴾, that is, My admonition.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 31:

When He knew that the mind of the attentive questioner was free, He resumed His speech with emphasis, as an indication that their punishment is something that is enjoyed and through which one attains success, and as a humbling of those who find it far-fetched that a single admonition should be followed by such an act, and as an informing that the power to punish those among others who denied is like the power to punish them, so there is no sense in denial: ﴿Indeed We﴾, with the greatness that is Ours, ﴿sent﴾ a mighty sending, and He indicated that it was a punishment by His words: ﴿upon them a Cry﴾. He belittled their affair in comparison with the magnitude of their punishment by His words, exalted is He: ﴿a single one﴾. Jibril, peace be upon him, cried it out against them, so there was no strength in this cry of his, which was a single one, and their clamour vanished before it, when they called upon their companion to hamstring the she-camel. When their destruction resulted from it, He said: ﴿So they became﴾ a state (p-123) of great magnitude ﴿like the crumbled refuse of the one who fences⦆ — that is, shattered like dry tree-wood which the shepherd, and whoever is in his position among those who make something to shelter in, keep, and protect their livestock with at a time when they have no shelter; it is his enclosure, that is, a circular barrier at that time for whoever enters into it. So it breaks and shatters, much of it, while he is building it, and the sheep trample it, then it shatters bit by bit. Everything that fell from it and was trampled by the sheep became hashim (crumbled refuse), and it is like the dry grass which the owner of the enclosure gathers for his livestock.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 32:

Since the implied sense is: "Indeed We have made the admonition abundantly clear to everyone who hears this story," he connected to it, emphasizing it for the sake of those who turn away from this Qur'an and justify their turning away by its difficulty, His words: ﴿And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy﴾, i.e., by what We possess of power and majesty, ﴿the Qur'an﴾, i.e., the Book that gathers every good and distinguishes between every confusion, ﴿for remembrance﴾, i.e., for memorization, reminding, being reminded, attaining distinction through it, and elevation in both abodes. And since this is the utmost in obligating turning toward it for all who turn away, He said: ﴿So is there anyone who will remember?﴾, i.e., anyone who looks into it, because of what We have said, with the eye of fairness and freedom from desire, so that he sees all that We have informed of, and We will help him to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 33:

When the warning (al-nadhir) was complete, it is as if he said to those warned what they had not heeded with it, so he increased their admonition. The story of Lut, peace be upon him, with his people was among the greatest of what came after Thamud, of what the Arabs know through reports and by seeing the remains (al-athar), and along with what their story contains of depicting the Hour, of the earth being changed into other than the earth, he resumed his statement: ﴿The people of Lut denied the warnings﴾, meaning: while they were in great strength regarding what they attempted, even though in this denial of theirs there was a weakness in the occurrence of women's stepping back from the same, as indicated by the feminine form of the verb with the ta' (ta'nith), and likewise (p-124) the stories preceding it. ﴿With the warnings﴾, meaning: the warning and the warnings and the warners. It indicates the extreme vileness of their transgression by putting first the report of their punishment, so he said:

﴿Indeed We﴾, meaning by the majesty that belongs to Us, ﴿sent﴾. The phrase ﴿upon them﴾ indicates that it was a sending of humiliation, and it also indicates their abasement and that His command reached everything intended by it, through His words ﴿a storm of stones﴾. That is, a wind that hurls stones smaller than pebbles (*hasib*, a storm-wind). It was destructive to them, scorching, sinking, and scattering. ﴿Except the family of Lot﴾, who were those who believed in him and were such that, when you saw him, it was as if you had seen Lot, peace be upon him, because of what appeared upon him of his deeds and of his walking in his manner in his words, his states, and his actions.

Since their exception implied their being saved, while leaving open the possibility that something might be sent upon them that was not restricted to what was mentioned, He said, beginning a new sentence as an answer to one who might be understood to have asked, "What was their condition?": ﴿We delivered them﴾, meaning a great deliverance, gradually. He mentioned the beginning of the process of their deliverance, saying ﴿at dawn﴾, meaning at the end of one of the nights, namely the night in which his people were punished. The indefiniteness (*tankir*) of the word is because we do not know that night precisely. Had you intended the dawn of the night from which morning came, the word would have been definite and would not take nunation, that is, it would be *ma'rifa la yanṣarif* (a definite form that is not declined with tanwin). *Saḥar* means the last sixth of the night, the time at which a person, especially women and children, is in the utmost state of heedlessness through being absorbed in sleep. In it God opens the gates of heaven by the permission of supplication, so that answering may occur from Him, because when kings open their doors, that is a permission for people to enter to fulfill their needs. Thus descent and the opening of gates is a metaphor (*kināya*) for that. God, glorified and exalted, is far above needing a descent, an opening of a gate, or anything else.

(p-125) Since what is meant by "those who warn" is obedience, which is the cause of salvation, He said, mentioning the favour and expressing it by its ultimate purpose, making known that His retribution is justice and His preservation is grace, because no one can repay His favours or any single one of them, and giving the reason for the salvation: ﴿a favour from Us﴾, meaning great and extraordinarily wondrous, for their gratitude. And since it was as if it were said, "Is this deliverance from among the wrongdoers specific to them?", and it is specific to them, He answered with His saying: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning like this great deliverance, which We made a recompense for them, ﴿We reward﴾ by Our power and Our greatness ﴿whoever gives thanks﴾, meaning whoever performs gratitude in all its kinds, so he believes and obeys, not... by enjoining good and forbidding evil, whoever he may be, whether a commoner or a ruler, tyrannical or just, brave or cowardly, for indeed We reward him with deliverance after the destruction of his enemy. Al-Qushayri said: "Gratitude for blessings of averting harm is more complete than gratitude for blessings of bringing benefit, and none knows that except every successful, intelligent person." So the verse is of _ihtibak_ (a rhetorical device in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa): He mentioned the favour first, because it is the true cause, as an indication of its omission second, and He mentioned gratitude second, because it is the apparent cause, as an indication of its omission first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 36:

Since the purpose here is to repel obstinacy, ... the listener's eagerness to know what his ﷺ (ﷺ) conduct was with them before the punishment: he had exceeded in thanking Us by warning them, advising them, and calling them to Us, returning what We had bestowed upon him of the message in its most complete forms. He linked to it, by way of allusion, His saying, emphasizing because the persistence in what is feared of punishment, while remaining in what necessitates it, is nearly unbelievable: ﴿And he had certainly warned them﴾, that is, Our messenger Lut (peace be upon him), ﴿of Our seizing﴾, that is, Our taking of them, coupled with the severity of the greatness that belongs to Us. He used the singular to indicate that nothing of His punishment, glory be to Him, is to be taken lightly; rather, a single seizing is sufficient given the greatness that belongs to Us, so it does not need the dual. (p-126) It also indicates that his warning was worthy of acceptance, because it was clear in its reality, by what follows from it in His saying: ﴿But they disputed﴾, that is, they strained to entertain weak doubt, ﴿about the warnings﴾, that is, the warning as a verbal noun, and the warnings or the warners, until it led them to denial, and so it was the cause of the seizing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 37:

When the failure to take precautions in devising a stratagem to escape the warning of the warner was a great established trait of foolishness, it indicated that they had gone beyond that to violating the sanctity of the warner. So He said, swearing an oath, because such a thing hardly ever happens and so the one who reports it would not be believed: ﴿And they had sought to seduce him﴾, meaning: they added to their denial, which necessitated punishment, a lengthy process of attempts that required maneuvering and turning about, ﴿from his guests﴾, in order to hand them over to them, and they were angels in the form of beardless youths. The plural is used though the intended sense is the category, to magnify the matter, as it would be if the guest were one person. ﴿So We obliterated﴾, meaning: as a consequence of their attempt to seduce him, We, by Our might, obliterated ﴿their eyes﴾, leveling them with the rest of the faces, so that no slit remained visible. Al-Baghawi said: this is the statement of most of the exegetes, and it was by a slap which Jibril, upon him be blessings and peace, dealt them. al-Qushayri said: he wiped over their faces with his wings, so they became blind and could not find the way out. Ibn Jarir said: the Arabs say, "The wind obliterated the landmarks," when it buries them with the dust it blows over them. So they fled hurriedly toward the door, unable to find it or to reach it, but colliding with the walls, out of fear of what was greater than that, while they were saying, "Lut's household are the most sorcerous of people." Their intellects did not lead them to believe and so save themselves from what had befallen them. al-Qushayri said: (p-127) Likewise, Allah, glory be to Him, has established His custom regarding His friends, by obscuring the hearts of their enemies until it becomes confused for them how to harm His friends and how He delivers them from their plotting. And when ... the first of their punishment, He said: ﴿So taste﴾, meaning: as a consequence of that someone said, on behalf of Allah, through the tongue of speech or of circumstance: "O deniers, taste ﴿My punishment and warnings﴾ because of your denial of My messengers in their warnings", meaning: and the outcome of My warning through the tongues of My messengers.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 38:

Since their remaining in disbelief after this was a wonder, for custom dictates that whoever is seized (by punishment) becomes restrained, even if he were the most wicked of creatures, and seeks pardon for himself, whether truthfully or falsely, through deception and cunning, so that he may be freed from what he is in... (they persisted) in holding fast to their denial, until they were punished in close proximity of time, He said, swearing an oath: ﴿And certainly there came upon them﴾, that is, it reached them at the time of morning, and He confirmed the meaning by His saying: ﴿early in the morning﴾, that is, at the beginning of the day, the punishment. Had the first part of your day, in which you are, been known, it would have been prevented...

﴿a punishment﴾, that is, the uprooting of their lands, lifting them up, then overturning them, pelting them with stones of fire, sinking them into the earth, and submerging them in foul water in which no living creature can survive. ﴿Settled﴾, that is, lasting upon them, not removed by illusion or sorcery as they said at the time of the effacing, for it destroyed them. It was then joined to the punishment of the barzakh, which is joined to the punishment of the Resurrection, which is joined to the greater punishment, in the tier that corresponds to their deeds, of the Fire. Then the tongue of their state said to them, if the tongue of speech did not speak:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 39:

﴿Taste﴾ — because of your deeds — ﴿My punishment and warnings.﴾

When he had repeated this refrain, it became clear that the cause of the punishment is denying the warning brought by any messenger whatsoever. And since the opening of each narrative serves as an alert that each of them is fit to be taken as a lesson [by them], it is understood that the implied meaning is: these admonitions have indeed reached their end for whoever has a heart. So He followed this with His words, reminding them of a blessing that has no equal: ﴿And We have indeed made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾. That is, exalted is our majesty and far-reaching is our glory, ﴿the Qur'an﴾, the comprehensive and the discerning, ﴿for remembrance.﴾ Had We willed, We could have raised it, by the greatness We possess, to such a degree that faculties would fall short of understanding it, just as We raised it to a rank where faculties stopped short of matching its composition. Or [We could have raised it to] a level of insight that does not cling to the hems of even the lowest of knowledge, except for a few of the most skilled of servants. How much more so, then, is what lies beyond that.

Since they still held back from hastening toward it and turning to it, He said, showing them gentleness and tenderness, giving the reason for this: ﴿So is there any one who will take heed?﴾ He emphasized it, saying: ﴿any who will take heed﴾, one who frees himself [from danger] by himself from the like of that into which these people have plunged themselves, thinking that the matter would not reach what it reached, out of ignorance on their part and their lack of concern for the consequences.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 41:

When the latter (generation) ought to beware of what befell the former, and the people of Pharaoh had come after the people of Lut, peace be upon him, it might be thought that they had not been warned, because whoever knows that the custom has been that those who denied the messengers were destroyed would deem it unlikely that denial would arise from those who followed that (generation). So He said, swearing an oath: ﴿And the family of Pharaoh had certainly come to them﴾, i.e., the king of the Copts in Egypt and his nobles, who, when seen, it was as if he were seen among them, because of their great closeness to him and their adopting his character. ﴿The warnings﴾, i.e., the admonitions, and those who warned with the warning of Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both. For the warning of some of the prophets is like the warning of all of them, since none of them came without having signs like those by which mankind believed, and the miracles are all equal in breaking the customary order. And Yusuf, peace be upon him, had warned them before.

When it was as if it were said, "What did they do when that came to them?", He said: ﴿They denied﴾, that is, with a great denial, treating them with contempt, ﴿Our signs﴾, which Moses, upon him be peace, and others brought to them, because of their denial of them, despite the greatness that they possess, which definitively makes known [that] they are from Us.

Since extraordinary events (khawariq al-'adat, events that break the customary order) were, as has passed, equal in their footing in indicating the truthfulness of the one who brings them, and they had resolved that whatever sign he brought them, they would deny it, it was as if every sign had come to them. Therefore He said: ﴿all of them﴾. He made the following a consequence of that statement: ﴿So We seized them﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, in a manner similar to that by which We seized the people of Noah through drowning, ﴿a seizing of One Mighty﴾, that is, nothing overcomes Him while He overcomes everything, ﴿Omnipotent﴾, that is, He does not hasten the seizing, because He does not fear escape and does not dread a successor to His judgment, and His power reaches a degree whose reality description cannot grasp. For the form ifti'al (the morphological pattern of the verb, here akhadh, in its reflexive-augmented form) is based on haste, and whoever hastens an action reveals his own ignorance of it; so this [pattern] is in its most complete sense. This final aim is the one intended and nothing else. Thus it is an illustration (tamthil), since He, glorified is He, addresses us in terms of what we worship. With this emphasis, not one of them was spared. The narratives have been concluded with a similar description to that with which they were opened, namely the punishment of the corrupters by drowning, so that the conclusion corresponds to the beginning. The salvation of the righteous among the earlier people was by the ship, and the salvation of the righteous among the later people was by the land of the sea, which was their ship, so that the conclusion is greater than the beginning, as is the way of those who possess power.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 43:

When these admonitions reached their conclusion and their feet rose to the rank of al-Suha (the faint star), (p-130) and this did not make the disbelievers of Quraysh desist from their aversion, nor did it slacken their obstinacy and stubbornness, the tongue of their state was saying: "We do not fear anything of this." So the situation called for it to be said to them, as a binding of proof: ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾ — you who are firmly rooted in disbelief and steadfast upon it, O you who deny this noble Prophet, who conceal the suns of his religion. ﴿Better﴾ in this world in strength and numbers, or in religion before Allah, or before people, ﴿than those﴾, that is, the great disbelievers, the tyrants, the mighty ones whom We admonished you about in this surah, so that this would be a cause for the separation of your condition from theirs, so that you might feel safe from the punishment, despite the common bond of denial, even though you have no immunity from Allah. ﴿Or do you have﴾ — all of you, apart from them, your disbelievers and your non-disbelievers — ﴿an immunity﴾ from the punishment from Allah ﴿in the scriptures﴾, that is, the books that come from Him, by which you have felt secure from punishment, even though they are better than you? So the verse is of the type of *ihtibak* (a figure of omission in which each half supplies what is omitted from the other): it mentions the superiority first, as evidence for its omission second, and the immunity second, as evidence for its omission first.

Now that they had reached this degree of persistence in disbelief, despite the far-reaching admonitions and the firm appeals, they deserved the greatest anger. So the address turned away from them, as a notice of this and as a humiliation and belittling of them, and as a turning toward the Prophet (ﷺ) for consolation. He said, linking to what is implied by the context: Do they claim, out of ignorance and stubbornness, any one of these two matters? ﴿Or do they say﴾, i.e., these people among whom you live, dealing with them gently in speech and words and with gracious forgiveness, in compliance with Our command and to magnify your station, yet they have treated you with contempt: ﴿We are a united host﴾, i.e., a single group that is greatly unified in its gathering, so it is at the utmost degree of cohesion and has no separation ﴿victorious﴾, i.e., over every one who (p-131) opposes it, because they are of one heart. The singular form is for the word "jami'un" (a host), and to convey this meaning; or that each of them is judged to be victorious.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 45:

Since the tongue of the situation (lisan al-hal) speaks clearly that they are saying: "All of this, which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?" and the like, and some of them said: "If we are raised, we will surely be given wealth and children," and there is no doubt that this was utterly impossible, given the victory of the believers over them despite their fewness and weakness, he resumed the answer with His saying: ﴿They will be defeated﴾, with the easiest of matters, by whatever defeater it might be, with a promise in which there is no breaking. The reading of the majority is in the passive voice, which conveys greatness in the manner of the speech of those who have power, so it is more eloquent than the reading of Ya'qub with the nun and the active voice, which indicates greatness explicitly. ﴿The multitude﴾, whose gathering was previously said to have been exaggerated, so Allah fulfilled His promise and they were defeated at the Battle of Badr and elsewhere in this world, soon after. They continued to weaken until their affair was extinguished and their secret was entirely gone. This is among the clear proofs of prophethood. ﴿And they will turn their backs﴾, meaning: their turning-away will occur, all of them, by this kind of thing, such that one of them is in charge of it while defeated, because in the state of defeat no kind of humility ever turned them, by which they might hope for choice. And each of the singular "the back" (al-dubur) and "the victorious" and the plural "those who turn" is more eloquent than if something else had been placed in its position, and more decisive against obstinacy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 46:

When this occurred in the world, and it was on the Day of Badr, and that was among the signs of prophethood, and perhaps some would have thought that this was the end, it was as if it were said: That is not the greatest promised time. ﴿Nay, the Hour﴾, the Resurrection, in which there is the greatest gathering and the greatest terror, ﴿is their promised time﴾, i.e., the greatest [promised time] for the recompense that was threatened (p-132) ﴿and the Hour is more calamitous﴾ than anything that can be imagined to occur in the world. It is an elative form (af'al tafdil) from al-da'hiya (calamity), which is a dreadful matter for which no cure can be found. ﴿and more bitter﴾, because its punishment for the disbelievers does not part from them or leave them.

When he had informed them of the Hour with this terrifying report, he gave its reason, swearing an oath for its people and briefly describing some of what awaits them at its arrival, with the words, emphasizing their [displayed] denial: ﴿Indeed, the criminals﴾, that is, those who sever what God has commanded to be joined, ﴿are in error﴾, that is, blindness from the right aim, through their denial of the Resurrection, an error that encompasses them and prevents their escape from the calamities of the Hour and other things, and prevents them from reaching any of the goals they now rely upon. ﴿And in a blaze﴾, that is, fires that kindle and blaze to the utmost degree of intensity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 48:

﴿On the Day﴾ i.e., on that promised Day, ﴿they will be dragged﴾ i.e., at that moment, constantly, in the most humiliating manner possible for them, by whoever is dragging them, ﴿into the Fire﴾ i.e., the one that is complete in its fiery nature, ﴿upon their faces﴾ because they will be in the utmost state of abasement and disgrace, as a recompense for what they used to do in humiliating the friends of God, the Exalted; and it will be said to them, by whatever speaker happens to be present: ﴿Taste﴾ i.e., because they have no protection and no zeal in any respect, ﴿the touch of Saqar﴾ i.e., the pain of direct contact with the fiery level that scorches by its heat, so that it burns the body and melts it, and its fat flows out, ... and its juice flows as the date-syrup flows and the juice of the fresh date, and for this reason the palm tree is called "misqar" (a palm that yields juice).

When He had informed them of the coming of the Hour and of what would befall them in it, as a recompense for their deeds, which He had decreed for them, and which are a veil with which they were content in pursuing their desires, and by which they argued for His approval, and since someone might have supposed that their persistence in disbelief was not by His will, glorified is He, He gave a reason for this, drawing attention to the fact that all of it is His act, and that its attribution to the servants is only through outward matters, by which the proof is established against them in the course of their customary ways. So He said: ﴿Indeed, We﴾, that is, with the greatness that is Ours (p-133) ﴿created everything﴾, that is, of created things, all of them, small and great.

Since this generalization in creation was something the accusative (naṣb) understood, He resumed His statement as an explanation of the hidden governing verb (al-ʿāmil al-maṭwiyy) and as an information that this entire creation is placed in a firm order and a decreed, settled matter: ﴿We created it according to a measure﴾, that is, by decree, wisdom, precise proportion, a determined apportionment, an exact ordering, and a firm arrangement, at a known time and a limited place, written in that Tablet before its occurrence, which the angels measure by time and other things, by counting and all kinds of measures. Thus not even the weight of an atom is lost from it, for there is no contender with Us, given the complete power and perfect knowledge that are Ours. So this punishment is by Our power and Our will; therefore be patient with it and be content with it, just as you were content with your evil deeds, and then argue against Our servants that they are Our will, with the like of His saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him]﴾ [al-Anʿam: 148]. He has thus brought you to what you see, and it has been revealed in the most complete revelation that nothing occurs contrary to Our purpose, and that no question of "why?" is asked about a thing We have decreed. Al-Razi said in al-Lawāmiʿ: "Quantity (al-kammiyya) is removed from His acts, just as modality (al-kayfiyya) and quantity are removed from His essence and His attributes." End.

Nothing of His command, glorified is He, occurs except what is in utmost wisdom. Had the creation not been raised after death, so that retribution and the just reckoning would take place, the reckoning would be random and not by measure and justice. For it is witnessed that corruption among the responsible persons in this abode outweighs righteousness many times over.

It is recorded as a non-canonical reading (shādhdh) with the nominative ("kull" read as "kullu") and Ibn Jinnī considered it stronger than the accusative. But this is not so, because the nominative does not convey what I have mentioned. What led him to that was only that he is a Muʿtazilī (adherent of the Muʿtazila, the rationalist school). The accusative, according to what I have determined, is a shattering blow to the Muʿtazila.

Having shown that everything happens by His act, he then showed how easy that is for Him and how effortless it is, so he said: ﴿And Our command is but one [single act]﴾, meaning that whatever We intend, however great its effect, is one act. He magnified the matter and belittled the things decreed by using the feminine form, so he said: ﴿but one [single act]﴾, that is, a single easy deed that involves no labour, and there is no producing of a saying (qawl) there, because the divine word is eternal (qadim). Rather, it is the connection of power (qudrah) to the thing decreed in accordance with the eternal will (irádah al-azaliyyah). Then he gave us an example of this with the swiftest thing the mind can grasp and the lightest, so he said: ﴿like a glance of the eye﴾. Just as the blink of one of you is no burden to him, so too are all acts, and indeed even easier than that.

When He had informed of the completeness of His power, and the destruction of the unbelievers mentioned and the deliverance of the righteous mentioned in this surah was somewhat like what He mentioned concerning the Hour in ease and swiftness, He indicated this by the deliverance of His allies and the destruction of His enemies. So He reminded by them collectively, and by what had been their conditions, with the easiest of matters, because that is more admonishing to souls and more restraining to minds. So He said, swearing an oath, drawing attention to their habit of disbelief despite this admonition, the act of one who denies, by their destruction on account of their denial, conjoining it to what is implied by the sense: "And We certainly delivered Our messengers and their followers from every grave matter." ﴿And We certainly destroyed﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿your counterparts﴾, those who you and they are one law in denial, and the power over you is like the power over them. So beware lest there befall you what befell them. Therefore He made the following consequent upon it: ﴿So is there anyone who will take heed?﴾, that is: from what befell them, that it is like what passed before them, rather many times over... and that His power, glorified is He, over it is like His power over them, so that he may turn back from his error out of fear of His might, glorified is He.

When the demonstration of the all-encompassing power over the awesome deeds that were witnessed, which no power other than His, glorified is He, could contain, was complete, and they had thought that His states were not controlled, because they cannot be controlled and no knower's knowledge can encompass them, especially when one claims that He is One, He began to complete the report of His greatness of power by informing that all their deeds are written down, let alone being preserved. So He said: ﴿And everything they have done is in the Zubur﴾, that is, the partisans (al-ashyā‘), at whatever time it was, is recorded in writing ﴿in the Zubur﴾, that is, in the books of the guardians (al-ḥafaẓa, the angels who record deeds). So let them beware of their deeds, for they are not forgotten. This is what the readers of the Qur'an (al-qurrā’) agreed upon, which led to this meaning through the nominative case of ﴿كُلُّ﴾ (kull). For if it were in the accusative, it would give the false impression that the prepositional phrase is governed by the verb, so that it would imply that they had done every kind of thing in the Zubur, and that is corrupt.

When He had particularized them, He generalized with His saying, admonishing, warning and cautioning, that every thing is preserved, then written down, then presented to the human being on the Day of Gathering: ﴿And every small and great thing﴾ of the substances and the meanings, from them and from others, ﴿is inscribed﴾, that is, written down in a magnificent manner, through the diligence of the guardians (al-hafazah) in writing it and setting it down accurately, along with the ease and facility of that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 54:

When he had informed about the conditions of the disbelievers in this world and the Hereafter, admonishing by them and making known His greatness, the loftiness of His attributes, the vastness of His dominion, and the all-encompassing scope of His knowledge and power, he concluded with the conditions of the other division of the people of the Hour, who are the people of His obedience, as a completion of that and as an indication and glad tidings for the wayfarer on the best of paths. So he said, emphasizing in response to the one who denies: ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ (al-muttaqun), that is, the excellent ones in the attribute of fear of Allah the Exalted, which led them to not do anything except with proof. And since gardens, water, and what is apparent are, by every measure, the opposite of the state of the astray one, far from the intended path (p-136), who is falling into destruction and the Fire, he said: ﴿in gardens﴾, that is, in orchards with trees that delight those within them. Al-Qushayri said: when a plural is set against a plural, the singulars correspond to the singulars. And since the gardens cannot stand nor endure except by water, he said: ﴿and a river﴾, and he made it singular because the expression with "fi" (in) conveys their being encompassed by it, an encompassing of the kind that is like a container in which they are contained; and because of the abundance and greatness of the rivers, to the point that, owing to the nearness of some to others, the connection of their sources, and the readiness of the whole land for the flowing of rivers from it, they are as though they were one thing. What is promised to the righteous of bliss in that abode has its subtle forms hastened for them in this abode. So for them today are gardens of knowledge and rivers of gnosis, and in the Hereafter, flowing rivers, meadows, trees, palaces, and adornments. It is also suitable, along with this, that it be of the kind from which daylight comes, so the meaning becomes: they are in light and expanse, never departing from it at all, in contrast to the condition of the criminal, who is in blindness arising from darkness. And for such purposes he used the singular while intending the genus, not merely for the sake of the rhyme (fasila).

In the Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 54, verse 55:

Since gardens are not inhabited in this world, because everything a person needs is not found in them, he (God) made clear that the state of those (gardens) differs from the state of this (world). So He said, substituting (this phrase) for what came before it: ﴿in a seat﴾, meaning those Gardens are the place of their residence, the seat where one sits for the purpose of sitting. ﴿Of truth﴾, meaning that in them the existence of what a person wishes for is true to the wish. Only the people of truth sit in it, and nothing in it is but its truth. There is ﴿no idle talk in it, nor any sinfulness﴾. The singular form is used to indicate the category, even though the substitution implies that there is no place in those Gardens that is not suitable to be named by this name. Also, because their hearts are united and they are content, they are ((p-١٣٧)) as if they were in one single seat, although it has also been read in the plural.

Since this was not customary, he made clear that its cause is God's granting them power over it, because of His special favour to them and His bringing them near, through His pleasure with them. So He said, qualifying this by the expression of nearness ("with") because His nearness, glorified and exalted is He, is free from the proximity of bodies and directions: ﴿with a Sovereign﴾, meaning a King of complete sovereignty, ﴿All-Powerful﴾, meaning of all-encompassing power, reaching a degree that no one other than Him, glorified is He, can comprehend, as was mentioned shortly before. So He brings them to every good and repels from them every harm. Just as they have the nearness of witnessing in the Hereafter, they have the nearness of support in this world. This noble name has a secret in victory over the wrongdoers. The surah has been concluded, as you see, just as it began, with the matter of the Hour. The beginning was for the beginning and the ending for the ending. The ending added an explanation of the cause that brings it into existence, which is His power, glorified is He and exalted is His majesty, and His mercy and beneficence are great, and His pardon, forgiveness and good pleasure. And because the people in it are divided into a disbeliever deserving retribution and a believer qualified for the utmost honour, He did not mention the greatest, all-comprehensive name, which is mentioned in the context requiring the combination of majesty and honour, for one category alone, namely the one from whom faith proceeds and who is not defiled by disobedience. These are ﴿those who believe﴾. Because it shares with the two surahs that follow it in this presentation, which is speech concerning the two categories only, without any incidental mention of those who believed, he placed the three together in being free of mention of the greatest name. So it did not mention it in any of them, and there came in them of attributes what requires greatness over the people of disbelief, and what indicates honour and beneficence for the people of faith: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman: 46]. For this reason this (surah) was concluded with the attribute of sovereignty, which requires complete dominance ((p-١٣٨)) and far-reaching honour, and indifference to anyone whoever he may be, because a king, insofar as he is a king, his station requires either the humiliation of the enemy or the honouring of the ally. He also made this in the form of emphasis. All of this is to inform that His management, glorified is He, of the affairs of the Hereafter, is as is intended in this surah in His management of the affairs of this world, by destroying the enemies and saving the allies. It seems that this surah was like this because it came after the surah of al-Najm, in which He explained the Night Journey (al-Isra'), and the Prophet (ﷺ) had greatness through breaking customary norms, by piercing the heavens and reaching the furthest limit of intimate conversation, and other things from the secret of the dominion and the place of might. This was after He had alluded to his station, peace and blessings be upon him, through (the mention of) al-Tur (Mount Sinai), so that the difference might be known and each might be described with what is true. This required that after him no one among people would be other than a pure believer; and if anyone were other than that, he would be a stubborn person of extreme disbelief. It seems that it was made three (surahs) to intend the utmost emphasis on this intense meaning. When the three were finished, this (name) was blessed in most of the verses of al-Hadid. Then every verse of al-Mujadila was crowned with it, as an indication that the utmost longing for it had been achieved, as a warning to whoever disobeys, especially whoever is an opponent, and as an encouragement to obedience to the King, the Forgiver. And God is the Granter of success in what He wills; indeed He is Strong, Doer of whatever He wills.
